questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Author presentation context: Which opening is strongest?

answer.text: A. "After the Rain" is a short prose piece meant to show a character who is safe but still unsure how to move forward.

feedback.text: Correct. This names title, form, and purpose. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: B. My story has a driveway, rain, and an umbrella, and then things happen.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This mostly summarizes events without purpose. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I do not know what my piece is about.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The author needs to frame the work clearly.

answer.text: D. The audience should figure out everything with no help.

feedback.text: Incorrect. An author presentation should provide a useful entry point.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which sentence best explains craft reasoning?

answer.text: A. I used an umbrella because umbrellas exist.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain craft purpose. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. The story has words and sentences.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too general. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I made choices because writing needs choices.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain a specific reader effect.

answer.text: D. I repeated the umbrella image so the reader could see the character holding onto protection even after the rain stopped.

feedback.text: Correct. This names the craft choice and explains reader effect.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which author presentation mistake should be corrected?

answer.text: A. Naming the purpose of the creative work.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Naming purpose is useful. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Retelling every event so the audience has no reason to read the piece.

feedback.text: Correct. The presentation should guide the audience, not replace the creative work.

answer.text: C. Explaining a revision decision.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Revision reflection strengthens the presentation. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Asking the audience to notice a repeated image.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This can prepare readers effectively. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which audience frame is strongest?

answer.text: A. Do not pay attention to anything.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not guide the audience. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. I will explain every symbol before you read.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This overexplains and may replace the creative experience.

answer.text: C. As you read, notice how the repeated umbrella image changes from protection to hesitation.

feedback.text: Correct. This gives the audience a specific craft feature to notice.

answer.text: D. The piece is about stuff.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is too vague. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L06_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.COM.01

Which revision reflection is strongest?

answer.text: A. I removed the sentence that named the feeling so the final action could show uncertainty instead of explaining it directly.

feedback.text: Correct. This names the change and explains why the final version is stronger.

answer.text: B. I changed it because revision was required.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This does not explain improvement. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. I changed random sentences for no reason.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Revision should be purposeful. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. I did not revise anything because first drafts are always final.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The course expects purposeful revision. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.
